tagline: A scenic connector joins the interstate to the Lowcountry’s changing road network.
intro: The Hilton Head Scenic Highway follows the connector east from I-95 in Jasper County toward Beaufort County. At Hardeeville, the setting is the Atlantic coastal plain, with little change in elevation. US 278 carries heavy traffic between the interstate, Bluffton and Hilton Head Island. The state designation prohibits off-premises outdoor advertising along the scenic highway.

The connector received its scenic-highway name in 1988. US 278 moved onto the route in 1996–1997, running south to Hardeeville and then east to SC 170. Its former course became portions of SC 336 and SC 462.
Start at I-95’s Exit 8 in Hardeeville and follow US 278 east toward SC 170. Beyond SC 170, the separately designated Hilton Head Island Scenic Byway continues to Sea Pines Circle on the island.

moments.title: Purrysburg
moments.text: Purrysburg occupied the South Carolina bank of the Savannah River, northwest of present-day Hardeeville. Jean-Pierre Purry led the first settlers and used enslaved labor. Its settlers were primarily French- and German-speaking Swiss Protestants from Neuchâtel and Geneva. By 1736, the town had 100 houses and as many as 450 settlers. Disease and overlapping land grants troubled the settlement; over the following decades, many residents left for other towns in South Carolina or Georgia. The town was abandoned. Archaeologists later investigated its site, including work by the LAMAR Institute on the Revolutionary War battlefield.

moments.title: Hardeeville
moments.text: A depot and general store helped turn this settlement into Hardee’s Station. Whyte William Hardee, son of settler Isaac Hardee, brought those businesses to the Charleston and Savannah Railway. The name became Hardeeville when the town was founded in 1911. Argent Lumber Company used three-foot-gauge tracks to move timber out of the swamps for transfer to standard-gauge railcars or trucks. As logging declined, US 17 and then I-95 brought commerce serving motorists. Argent donated its Number 7 steam locomotive to the city for display in 1960. The city lists the engine among its community facilities at Hardeeville Veterans Park.

moments.title: St. Luke's Church
moments.text: St. Luke’s Church combines Georgian and Greek Revival architecture in a building constructed in 1824. The original Episcopal congregation had worshipped in a different building from 1786, on land donated by John Bull. John Guerard provided the site for the present church on former Bull Hill Plantation land. The church was sold to Methodists in 1875, and they continue to use it. The building retains galleries built for enslaved worshippers and entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1987. The church stands in rural Beaufort County, about four miles north of Pritchardville.
